extraction.name: CoNLL-2003 Named Entity Recognition Dataset
extraction.description: A dataset for language-independent named entity recognition covering English and German, with training, development, test, and unannotated data files. Named entities are tagged as persons (PER), organizations (ORG), locations (LOC), and miscellaneous (MISC) using the IOB tagging scheme.
extraction.creator: Erik F. Tjong Kim Sang and Fien De Meulder, CNTS - Language Technology Group, University of Antwerp
extraction.citeAs: Tjong Kim Sang, E. F. and De Meulder, F. (2003). Introduction to the CoNLL-2003 Shared Task: Language-Independent Named Entity Recognition. arXiv:cs/0306050v1
extraction.rai:dataCollection: English data was taken from the Reuters Corpus (news stories between August 1996 and August 1997). German data was taken from the ECI Multilingual Text Corpus, specifically from the German newspaper Frankfurter Rundshau, from articles written in one week at the end of August 1992.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: English: Reuters Corpus (Reuters news stories). German: ECI Multilingual Text Corpus (German newspaper Frankfurter Rundshau).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: English: August 1996 to December 1996 (training/dev from end of August 1996, test from December 1996, raw data from September 1996). German: August 1992 to December 1992 (training/dev/test from one week at end of August 1992, raw data from September to December 1992).
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A tokenizer, part-of-speech tagger, and chunker were applied to the raw data. English data was tagged and chunked by the memory-based MBT tagger. German data was lemmatized, tagged and chunked by the decision tree tagger Treetagger.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Named entity tagging of English and German training, development, and test data was done by hand at the University of Antwerp. Mostly, MUC conventions were followed. An extra named entity category called MISC was added to denote all names which are not already in the other categories.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: MBT tagger (for English POS tagging and chunking), Treetagger (for German lemmatization, POS tagging and chunking)
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Named entities are assumed to be non-recursive and non-overlapping. When a named entity is embedded in another named entity, usually only the top level entity has been annotated.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, development, and testing of named entity recognition systems. The dataset was used in the CoNLL-2003 shared task for developing machine learning-based named entity recognition systems for English and German.

name.evidence: We describe the CoNLL-2003 shared task: language-independent named entity recognition. We give background information on the data sets (English and German) and the evaluation method

description.evidence: The CoNLL-2003 named entity data consists of eight files covering two languages: English and German. For each of the languages there is a training file, a development file, a test file and a large file with unannotated data.

url.evidence: Data files (except the words) can be found on http://lcg-www.uia.ac.be/conll2003/ner/

creator.evidence: Erik F. Tjong Kim Sang and Fien De Meulder, CNTS - Language Technology Group, University of Antwerp

publisher.evidence: We describe the CoNLL-2003 shared task: language-independent named entity recognition.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: The English data was taken from the Reuters Corpus. This corpus consists of Reuters news stories between August 1996 and August 1997. The text for the German data was taken from the ECI Multilingual Text Corpus. The portion of data that was used for this task, was extracted from the German newspaper Frankfurter Rundshau.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: The English data was taken from the Reuters Corpus. This corpus consists of Reuters news stories between August 1996 and August 1997. The text for the German data was taken from the ECI Multilingual Text Corpus.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: The English data was taken from the Reuters Corpus. This corpus consists of Reuters news stories between August 1996 and August 1997. The text for the German data was taken from the ECI Multilingual Text Corpus. The portion of data that was used for this task, was extracted from the German newspaper Frankfurter Rundshau.

rai:dataCollectionTimeframe.evidence: For the training and development set, ten days' worth of data were taken from the files representing the end of August 1996. For the test set, the texts were from December 1996. The preprocessed raw data covers the month of September 1996. All three of the training, development and test sets were taken from articles written in one week at the end of August 1992. The raw data were taken from the months of September to December 1992.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: The participants were given access to the corpus after some linguistic preprocessing had been done: for all data, a tokenizer, part-of-speech tagger, and a chunker were applied to the raw data. We created two basic language-specific tokenizers for this shared task. The English data was tagged and chunked by the memory-based MBT tagger (Daelemans et al., 2002). The German data was lemmatized, tagged and chunked by the decision tree tagger Treetagger (Schmid, 1995).

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: Named entity tagging of English and German training, development, and test data, was done by hand at the University of Antwerp. Mostly, MUC conventions were followed (Chinchor et al., 1999). An extra named entity category called MISC was added to denote all names which are not already in the other categories.

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: The English data was tagged and chunked by the memory-based MBT tagger (Daelemans et al., 2002). The German data was lemmatized, tagged and chunked by the decision tree tagger Treetagger (Schmid, 1995).

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: We assume that named entities are non-recursive and non-overlapping. When a named entity is embedded in another named entity, usually only the top level entity has been annotated.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: The learning methods were trained with the training data. The development data could be used for tuning the parameters of the learning methods. When the best parameters were found, the method could be trained on the training data and tested on the test data.
